pr_body:
Fix #113763 by:
* Fix informers to track HasSynced properly
* propagate HasSynced to each Handle individually
* Add AsyncTracker to help multi-worker controllers track whether they've synced or not


/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Plumbs the fact of whether an item was in the initial list or not to controllers, where they can choose to track whether they have processed it or not.

```release-note
Shared informers now correctly propagate whether they are synced or not. Individual informer handlers may now check if they are synced or not (new HasSynced method). Library support is added to assist controllers in tracking whether their own work is completed for items in the initial list (AsyncTracker).
```

kube-scheduler also needs this to reliably schedule pods. Currently, it is possible that we start scheduling before adding all nodes or pods into the scheduler cache/snapshot. That can lead to pods scheduled into non-optimal nodes in the best case, or oversubscribe nodes in the worst case.

> kube-scheduler also needs this to reliably schedule pods. Currently, it is possible that we start scheduling before adding all nodes or pods into the scheduler cache/snapshot. That can lead to pods scheduled into non-optimal nodes in the best case, or oversubscribe nodes in the worst case.

The size of our internal cluster is very large and we encountered this kind of problem. In order to solve this problem, some of our internal components list all the data and do some initialization logic after the Informer synchronization is completed.
Some scheduling plugins need to maintain some state by themselves to achieve some efficient scheduling capabilities, and some complex plugins require multiple Informers to construct these states, and it is also expected to have such a synchronization mechanism to ensure the correctness of the state.

Here is how we ended up using this btw:

https://github.com/istio/istio/blob/17f494092f5f6c8fbfc48de09551fb0725d8edde/pkg/kube/kclient/client.go#L155-L168

Small wrapper around Informer that keeps track of the handlers added via the wrapper and waits for them as part of HasSynced.

Not sure if the implementation of this place will have a race condition. For example, after the Cache data synchronization is completed, the EventHandler is registered. At this time, it traverses the data in the Cache, initiates an addNotification and calls syncTracker.Start, then syncTracker.count becomes to 1. When the addNotification is consumed, execute syncTracker.Finish, then syncTrakcer.count becomes to 0, just at this time an external goroutine called syncTracker.HasSynced, because upstream hasSynced, and syncTracker.count = 0, so syncTracker.HasSynced returns true.

Maybe can consider passing the total number of objects in the Cache directly to syncTracker.count before initiating addNotification.

We hold the lock on the informer while adding these, which means no one can call the informer's HasSynced method untill we have added them all, which also means the handler's HasSynced method can't be called, since it calls the informer's HasSynced method. I can expand the comment here.

However now that you mention it I need to fix up the tracker to check things in the other order, I think.

Yes... I overlooked that..😅

My understanding is `isInInitialList` means "this is from the initial list".

The issue I have as a consumer is that I still can't tell when the initial list is _done_. I can't wait for an Add with `isInInitialList=false`, because there may never be one.

I would have expected this to be `isLastItemInList := f.hasSynced_locked()` (at L539, not here). Then a consumer can handle in their add controller `if isLastItemInList { do what I want on sync }`.

This may also lean towards having an `OnInitiallListCompleteFunc()` callback rather than a bool in the `AddFunc`, but that is stylistic - I don't have a strong preference

What you describe won't work because eventually people start doing work async, knowing the last one isn't helpful, you need to know every one that's still in flight.

I will show how to use this in at least one controller.

The final check is going to look like `informer.HasSynced() && !initialListItems.InFlight()`, the latter part isn't in this PR yet.

My thinking was that each layer needs to propagate some notion of "done". Anytime you add async, you are breaking that, and need to add it back at that layer. The goal of this is to propogate it at the informer handler layer. If you have _another_ layer on top of that (multiple worker queues, in k8s typically), then you will need some higher level solution on top of that which can be done by just knowing once all the event handlers have been called. _how_ exactly to do that depends on the code on top of the informer.

Its a bit hard to discuss the final check since I may be misunderstanding the intended flow, but I am guessing it is keeping track of all the items that come in with isInInitialList=true and then removing them as the queue completes?
 
If so, IMO it would still be preferable to flip the logic. 

If users are using multi worker queues, they _can_ still do this by just keeping track of items that come in before OnInitiallListCompleteFunc triggers. But for users who don't have this setup, they shouldn't have to pay the complexity of tracking items when a simple callback will do IMO.
Users that aren't doing anything async already don't have any problems, so I don't understand why I shouldn't optimize it for people that are doing async things?

(BTW I agree having a separate function to call on completion of the initial list would be better if we were starting from scratch, but I think what I've done here is going to have more minimal changes for consumers)

This might just be a terminology thing - but I am not sure my understanding aligns with yours on non-async being ok as is.

When I am referring to non-async handlers, I mean something like this: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/57eb5d631ccd615cd161b6da36afc759af004b93/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/admission/configuration/mutating_webhook_manager.go#L100, while an async handler is typically `queue.Add`.

With that definition, non-sync users are still broken - they still cannot tell when they are fully synced because the informer internals are also async and don't expose a way to know when the initial list is complete (leading to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113761).

> more minimal changes for consumers

My initial thought was just adding a field to `ResourceEventHandlerFuncs`; adding a field seems like its backwards compatible in almost all cases except the cases of keyless struct initialization, which seems rare. But I didn't dig into it much, so maybe there is more issues?

---

To be clear - I think this works and I am far happier to have this than nothing, consider these nitpicks :slightly_smiling_face:

.... that code does N*log(N) work on start up for N webhooks, that's really bad, wow.

It appears to be wrong because HasSynced is called on the shared part of the informer, but not all notifications have made it through to the non-shared stub? That seems like a separate problem that I can also fix.

Yeah fundamentally its broken because it assumes HasSynced means "handler has been called for everything in initial state" but in reality it means "underlying store is synced"; this controller doesn't care about the underlying store since it maintains its own index on top of things.

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/113763 is really just about exposing a `HasHandlersBeenCalledWithInitialState()` logic (in some form), so that controllers like that (and others; this applies to things not doing NlogN logic..) can simply swap out their `informer.HasSynced()` logic (broken) with a similar semantic that is not broken

> this controller doesn't care about the underlying store since it maintains its own index on top of things

Specifically the problem is the lag -- shared informer pipes everything through a channel, HasSynced is correct except for the stuff sitting in that channel. If this were using a non-shared informer it'd actually be correct; in that case HasSynced won't return true until after your Add handler for the last initial item has returned.

NewFilteredPodInformer still makes a shared informer: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ea0764452222146c47ec826977f49d7001b0ea8c/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/informers/core/v1/pod.go#L58-L59

It still may not be ideal since now unrelated handlers can block each other though (not a concern for my personal use cases, but I can see how that would be for some users).

TIL that `!hasSynced` here doesn't necessarily mean that we're part of the initial list - the delta FIFO will be "synced" if anyone calls `Add/Update/Delete/AddIfNotPresent`. 

I did a quick pass through the reflector code and while it's true that it will synchronously `Replace()` everything in the initial list, I don't see it waiting for sync before starting to process `Watch()` events. Are we certain that it's not possible for delta FIFO to return `true` for HasSynced before all items in the list have been processed?

Things can't get demoted/preempted in the queue, so I think this isn't a problem?

A future change could get merged with a change from the initial list, if you don't want that you have to use the regular fifo. But most uses do want that, since it's more efficient.

Why is the queue important? My read was that `f.populated` was global? I'm considering the case where:

1. `*Reflector.syncWith()` calls `*DeltaFIFO.Replace()` for all items in the original list
1. `*Reflector.ListAndWatch()` begins the watch
1. `*controller.processLoop()` begins calling `*DeltaFIFO.Pop()` to process them
1. `*Reflector.watchHandler()` calls `*DeltaFIFO.Add()` with some new object it saw in the watch stream
1. `*controller.processLoop()` finishes using `*DeltaFIFO.Pop()` to consume all objects from the initial list

The delta FIFO `HasSynced()` would return `true` after 4, even though the initial list had not been processed yet, right? Since `f.populated` gets latched once `Add()` is called. The controller relinquishes the FIFO's lock between each `Pop()`, so the `Add()` could be interleaved?
`populated` is already set to true at the end of Replace()? It's initialPopulationCount going to zero that determines when it is synced.
Ah, jeez, sorry - I took the comment on `HasSynced` at face value and didn't realize `Replace()` also set it. Sorry for the noise!
